solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unhappily citified beast forgetting It's De-Lovely

definitions.note: beatific means blissful, radiantly happy: lovely in a heavenly way

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of citified beast are thrown into disorder
forgetting tells us some letters of the jumble are left behind: those spelling it's de

explanation.surface: A town-bred beast, unhappy, cannot remember the Cole Porter song It's De-Lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'Unhappily' jumbles CITIFIEDBEAST, and 'forgetting' removes the letters of IT'S DE from that pool. The Porter title It's De-Lovely is split between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatific describes a blissful, saintly radiance, the heavenly sort of beauty one might call lovely.

clue.text: Learning code in volume

indicators.note: in places the code's letters inside the word for a volume

parts.note: an edition is a published volume of a book
RU is rugby union, one of the football codes

explanation.surface: Studying a computer code printed in a large book.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the different forms of football are called codes; RU is Rugby Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarship, the knowledge acquired through study.

clue.text: Shelter on hill top tomorrow

definitions.note: the puzzle appeared on 9 June, so the next day is the tenth

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, taken from hill

explanation.surface: Plans to pitch a tent on the summit tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition depends on the publication date: the puzzle ran on 9 June 2016, Cole Porter's 125th birthday, so tomorrow was the tenth.
explanation.definitionFit: On a puzzle printed on the ninth of the month, the following day's date is the tenth.

clue.text: In France, Do I Love You's ill- tempered

parts.note: to do is to act
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
you, taken as a group, can be us; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: In France, the Porter song Do I Love You? is a cross one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Porter title Do I Love You? is broken into four pieces: ACT, I, O, US.
explanation.definitionFit: Fractious describes someone irritable and quarrelsome, easily put out of temper.

clue.text: Cleaner Ruby Black

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
ruby is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A cleaner called Ruby Black, named like a person.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a full name, but each word does its own job; Black is the definition, as in burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Charred means scorched until blackened, so black is a fair synonym.

clue.text: See 23 down
Some progress for monsters

indicators.note: some of means only a part of the word progress is used, the run inside it

explanation.surface: A little advance made against the monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are giant man-eating creatures of fairy tales, a kind of monster.

clue.text: So In Love? On the contrary with spiritual leader of many

indicators.note: in, with the contrary reading, puts the love letter inside the word for so
on the contrary flips So In Love so that love goes inside so instead

parts.note: thus means so, in that way
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
with means and, along with

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, taken from spiritual

explanation.surface: Is a spiritual leader So In Love with many people? Not really.
explanation.walkthrough: The Porter title So In Love would put the word for so inside love; 'On the contrary' flips the containment so love goes inside so, giving THOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousands is used loosely to mean a great many, a huge number.

clue.text: Overweight person expands ribcage and starts performance

indicators.note: starts means the first letters of the words leading up to it are taken

explanation.surface: A heavy singer fills their chest before the show begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the large opera singer drawing breath; the initials of the first five words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged musical work, a performance in which the drama is sung.

clue.text: Old money of West Africa

definitions.meaning: a former British gold coin worth twenty-one shillings
a country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa, whose gold gave the coin its name

explanation.surface: Historic currency from West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The coin is named after the West African region whose gold was used to mint it; the country there bears the same name.

clue.text: Pilots broadcast succeeded in fencing me in

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the word for succeeded wraps around me

parts.note: won means succeeded, came out on top
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pilots were broadcast saying they had managed to fence the speaker in, echoing Don't Fence Me In.
explanation.walkthrough: The Porter song Don't Fence Me In is alluded to; 'in' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Airwomen are female aviators, women who fly aircraft as pilots.

clue.text: Sharp manoeuvres avoiding buying Anything Goes

parts.note: someone tight with money is mean and avoids buying anything
goes, as in a turn in a game, means turns

explanation.surface: Sharp manoeuvres while not purchasing in the musical Anything Goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Anything Goes is Porter's musical; only 'Goes' gives letters, and 'Anything' is padding from the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight turns are sharp changes of direction, abrupt manoeuvres in driving or flying.

clue.text: Delay support

definitions.meaning: a brace or prop, like a ship's mast rope or a corset stiffener

explanation.definitionFit: A stay is both a suspension of proceedings and a supporting rope or strut.

clue.text: Understood True Love

parts.note: right means true, correct
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Taken as the Porter song title True Love, then acknowledged.
explanation.walkthrough: True Love is a Porter song from High Society.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is an informal acknowledgement meaning okay, got it, message received.

clue.text: Stuffing ground rose into hyacinth borders on affectation

indicators.note: into places the rearranged flower inside the two letters around it
borders of a word are its first and last letters, here of hyacinth
ground means crushed, so the letters of rose are broken up

parts.note: an air is an affected manner, a put-on attitude

explanation.surface: Crushed rose petals placed among hyacinths, a showy floral display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil for the flowers but is the anagram signal; 'borders on' looks like a single phrase, but 'on' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair from horses' manes and tails was traditionally used as padding in upholstery and mattresses.

clue.text: Dig up Richard I's interminable letters

indicators.note: letters here points to the run of letters lying inside Richard I's interminable

explanation.surface: Exhuming the endless correspondence of King Richard the Lionheart.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of Richard, I'S and the start of interminable, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinter is to exhume, to dig a buried body or object out of the ground.

clue.text: Superhero at odds with I've Got [name] Under My Skin

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the letter for name below the word for skin

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
I've, I have, supplies the letter I
derma is skin, as in dermatology

explanation.surface: A superhero quarrels with the song I've Got You Under My Skin, with a name inserted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Porter title I've Got You Under My Skin has 'You' replaced by a bracketed [name].
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is the Marvel comics hero with spider powers.

clue.text: Not including Just One Of Those Things? Answer: rash!

parts.note: ex means without, excluding, as in ex dividend
an means one, the indefinite article
them means those things, as a pronoun

explanation.surface: Leaving out the song Just One Of Those Things would be a rash answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like an adjective (hasty) but is the skin eruption. The Porter title Just One Of Those Things is the main fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An exanthema is a skin eruption accompanying a fever such as measles, a medical name for a rash.

clue.text: Charges department with decay and loses heart

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department
rust is decay of iron

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of loses

explanation.surface: A department is charged with neglect and loses its spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' is a verb here: hands into someone's keeping.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a task is to entrust it to them; both verbs mean to commit to another's care.

clue.text: Maybe gluttony treats cavities

parts.note: gluttony is one of the seven deadly sins, an example of a sin
to treat something in a certain way is to use it

explanation.surface: Overindulging in sweet treats leads to cavities in the teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavities' suggests tooth decay; the definition is the hollow spaces in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: The sinuses are air-filled hollows in the bones of the face, cavities around the nose.

clue.text: Connect Stalin with two disturbed characters

indicators.note: two of Stalin's characters are disturbed, moved from the end of the name round to the front

explanation.surface: Linking Stalin with a pair of unhinged figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters of STALIN move, to the front, which is why the clue says two characters.
explanation.definitionFit: To instal (a British spelling) equipment is to set it up and connect it.

clue.text: Incline to turn attention to following Begin The Beguine

indicators.note: following puts the turned word after the initial letter
begin points to the first letter of Beguine
to turn means the word for attention is read backwards

parts.note: ear means attention, as in lend an ear

explanation.surface: Inclined to give attention to the Porter song Begin the Beguine.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAE is a Scottish word for a hillside or slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A brae, in Scottish usage, is a steep bank or hillside, an incline.

clue.text: Form of mantra sung in Red, Hot and Blue

indicators.note: sung in places the chanted syllable inside the letters for the three colours and heat

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for red
H is hot, as on a tap
B is the abbreviation for blue, as in pencil grades
om is the sacred syllable chanted as a mantra

explanation.surface: A mantra chanted in Porter's musical Red, Hot and Blue.
explanation.walkthrough: A rhomb is a geometric shape; the 'and' of the title is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a geometric figure, a form with four equal sides.

clue.text: Hothead Cher often arranged From This Moment On

parts.note: the head of the word hot is its first letter, H

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of Cher often are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered Cher frequently arranged the Porter song From This Moment On.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hothead' looks like a person, but its head, H, is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforth means from now on, from this point onward.

clue.text: Singer of I Love Paris maybe performed only for thee

definitions.text: Singer of I Love Paris maybe

indicators.note: performed means these letters are played out in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer of the Porter song I Love Paris, performed just for you.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris here is the Trojan prince, not the city: she could sing I Love Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek queen famously loved the Trojan prince Paris, so she might sing that she loves him.

clue.text: Lungs could be source of piped music

definitions.meaning: a lung is an ... of the body
the pipe ..., an instrument that sounds through pipes

explanation.surface: Lungs might produce piped music.
explanation.definitionFit: Lungs are an example of a bodily organ, and the church organ sends music through pipes.

clue.text: Stars of Can-Can never left

indicators.note: left places the negative word to the left of the other piece

parts.note: not, like never, is a word of negation
can means able; two cans read as a plural give ables

explanation.surface: Stars of Porter's musical Can-Can never departed.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger left this unparsed; a commenter's reading is used: Can-Can as ABLES, with NOT placed on its left.
explanation.definitionFit: Notables are prominent people, the stars of a field or society.

clue.text: Bar that attracts certain elements

parts.note: a pub drawing particular sorts of people, or a bar of metal pulling iron and nickel

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pub with a dubious clientele; the elements are chemical ones such as iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar magnet attracts ferromagnetic elements like iron, cobalt and nickel.

clue.text: King's robe on askew

indicators.note: askew means crooked, so the letters of robe on are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: The king has put on his robe crookedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is from Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the King of the Fairies in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Relatively new title for groom

parts.note: relatively hints at family relations: the bridegroom gains a fresh family label on marrying

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean fairly, but it points to relatives: on marrying, the groom becomes his wife's parents' kin.
explanation.definitionFit: After the wedding the groom becomes the child-by-marriage of his bride's parents.
